chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The example of the violet (oil) among the oils is like the example of our Shias among the people.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor of violet oil in Shia hadith
ai.summary: In this well-known hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of violet oil (*banafsaj*) to illustrate the spiritual purity and distinctiveness of the Shia among the general populace. Just as violet oil is prized for its unique fragrance and quality amidst other oils, the Shia are characterized by their adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt and their elevated moral and spiritual status in the eyes of God. This narration underscores the concept of *tazkiyah* (purification) and the special standing of the faithful who maintain their identity through devotion to the Imams.
